## What this repository is, and what it is not

The engine is elsewhere and is not duplicated here: [https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kekkai](https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kekkai) is the control plane and [https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kekkai-node](https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kekkai-node)
is the data plane. This repository is the half of that engine which needs no
private key — policy evaluation and envelope verification — wrapped in an HTTP
envelope and a payment gate.

It signs nothing. Issuing a netmap means holding the authority key, and a Worker
reachable from the public internet is the wrong place to keep one.

## Why authorisation is the meter, and bandwidth cannot be

The engine's charter (G4) is that there is no `:traffic/*` and no
`:user/activity` namespace: the control plane authorises reachability and never
records what flows through the tunnels. A per-gigabyte overlay would have to
measure gigabytes, so it cannot be built on this engine without contradicting the
property that makes the engine worth using.

So the meter sits on **authorisation** — a decision the plane already makes and
already writes to its genealogy ledger. It is the only unit here that can be
counted without learning something the plane promised not to learn.

## What is free, and why that is a design decision

**`/netmap/verify`** — charging to check whether an artifact is authentic prices the one action that protects the buyer. A node that cannot afford to verify runs unverified, which is the failure this whole boundary exists to prevent.
